clue.text: Singer in church introduced by priest

indicators.note: a thing introduced by another has that other placed in front of it, so the priest's letters lead

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A chorister in church is presented to the congregation by the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a choirboy, but it is the pop star Prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince was the stage name of the American pop star, a singer and songwriter.

clue.text: Places to see uncles and fathers dance with sons

parts.note: pops is slang for fathers
a hop is an informal dance
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Dads and their boys dance together while visiting relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, and to pop something is to pawn it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop shops are pawnshops, run by the pawnbrokers nicknamed uncles.

clue.text: As far as I am concerned, it's a state in Nigeria

definitions.text: As far as I am concerned
definitions.meaning: the internet shorthand for in my opinion

explanation.surface: Someone personally insists that a place is part of Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for in my opinion, and is also the name of a Nigerian state.

clue.text: Soldier in Burma using Indian language in court

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: Hindi is a main language of India

explanation.surface: A soldier in Burma speaks an Indian tongue in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were a British-led special force fighting behind Japanese lines in Burma in the Second World War.

clue.text: Theatrical drummer discontented with violin concerto's introduction

indicators.note: with its contents taken out, only the outside letters of drummer remain

parts.note: an Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona

indicators.note: a piece's introduction is its opening, here the first letter of concerto's

explanation.surface: A grumpy drummer joins the violinist at the start of a concerto in some showy performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like the drummer's mood; it means emptied, leaving DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something theatrical is showy and full of effect, just as a dramatic gesture is.

clue.text: GI in dress abandoned formality?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An American soldier wearing a frock has ditched all stuffiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidness is stiffness or strictness, and formality is rule-bound stiffness; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Springtime gala in part of London

parts.note: May is a spring month
a fair is a festive gala

explanation.surface: A spring festival is held in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is an upmarket area of London's West End.

clue.text: Shopkeeper supplying damson and water concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A grocer sells a homemade drink of damsons and water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradeswoman is a woman in trade, such as one keeping a shop.

clue.text: Shrewd, getting a great deal in Cyprus

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
a raft of things is a great many of them

explanation.surface: A canny buyer finds a bargain in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a great deal' sounds like a bargain; it means a lot, RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning and astute, close to shrewd.

clue.text: Jamaican politician, perhaps, one lacking backbone

parts.note: a Jamaican, perhaps, is West Indian, abbreviated WI
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Caribbean politician turns out to be spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, cowardly person with no spirit.

clue.text: Concert, one alone showing great potential?

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
I is the Roman numeral for one
singly means one by one, alone

explanation.surface: A solo performer at a concert shows real promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are an annual series of London concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a way that shows great potential is doing it in a manner full of promise.

clue.text: Literary pieces regularly featured in annual

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of annual, from the first

explanation.surface: Short writings appear every so often in a yearly anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: Ana is a collection of literary sayings or anecdotes about a person, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Reported entire political party in hiding

indicators.note: a reported word is one heard spoken, so a soundalike of the word for entire is wanted

parts.note: entire means whole
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A news report says the entire party has gone underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'entire' is heard: 'whole' sounds like 'hole'. The DUP is a Northern Irish party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holed up is sheltering out of sight, an idiom for lying low.

clue.text: Chicken £49, plus delivery surprisingly

parts.note: £ is L, from libra, and 49 is IL in Roman numerals

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird costs forty-nine pounds plus postage, to the buyer's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the bird bought; it is an adjective meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-livered means cowardly, as does chicken used as an adjective.

clue.text: Each holiday to east of Germany is most precious

indicators.note: in an across answer, east is to the right, so these pieces come after the letter for Germany

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: Every break taken in eastern Germany is a treasured one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearest is the superlative of dear, which means precious or much loved.

clue.text: A drink knocked back with food — delicious

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but here the letters are turned round

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat
table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A quickly downed drink goes with a tasty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking; it turns A + LAP into PALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable food is pleasant to taste, a milder synonym of delicious.

clue.text: Beef dish brought round sailing vessel shortly

indicators.note: the dish's letters are brought round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person, a belle

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a yacht is a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A beef dish is carried round a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' and 'dish' suggest a meal; beef is a verb, to complain, and a dish is a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for to grumble, as is to bellyache.

clue.text: Resistance shown by wife during massive arguments

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: a thing occurring during another sits within it, so wife goes inside

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A wife's resistance shows up in some huge marital quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows, rhyming with cows, are noisy quarrels or disputes.

clue.text: Examiner interrupts classes sorrowfully

indicators.note: the answer breaks into the words that follow, lying hidden across them

explanation.surface: An inspector sadly breaks into lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is someone who evaluates or examines, such as an exam marker.

clue.text: Derek's rejected winter transport

indicators.note: rejected is read as thrown back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Del is the short form of Derek, so Derek's gives Del's

explanation.surface: Derek's form of winter travel has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled is a sledge, a vehicle on runners used over snow.

clue.text: Composer of French stories about British

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: about means around, so the stories surround the letter for British

parts.note: lies are stories, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: A composer writes French tales concerning Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was a French composer of the ballets Coppélia and Sylvia.

clue.text: Miss entertaining friend and mother in Spanish-speaking resort

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the girl's word surrounds the others

parts.note: a miss is a girl or lass
a pal is a friend
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A young woman hosts her friend and her mum at a Spanish holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas is the capital of Gran Canaria, a Spanish island holiday destination.

clue.text: Try trampoline initially during various team exercises

indicators.note: a thing occurring during another sits within it
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters are reordered
initially picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: Have a go on the trampoline while the team does various workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts T inside ATEM, the rearranged TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try, as a noun or a verb.

clue.text: Like short, cut flowers

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: a cut word loses its last letter

parts.note: terse means short or curt

explanation.surface: Cut flowers, like short ones, look neat in a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like garden flowers.

clue.text: Husband loyally leaves friend something to eat

parts.note: to husband resources is to save them

indicators.note: when the friend leaves, those letters depart from the word loyally

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A faithful husband walks out on his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is a verb, meaning to save. A saveloy is a spicy British sausage, often from chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a seasoned smoked sausage, so it is food, something to eat.

clue.text: Show chum round home at start of evening

indicators.note: the friend's word goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a mate is a chum
in means at home

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friend comes round to the house as the evening begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or film, a type of show.

clue.text: Repair last bit of motorway?

parts.note: M is a motorway, as in M1
the end is the last bit

explanation.surface: Fixing the final stretch of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of the M road reads as M END. British motorways are called M1, M25 and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to fix or repair it.

clue.text: Do wrong, stealing capital from German chap

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr, a man

explanation.surface: Robbing a German man of his money is a wicked act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is the initial H of HERR.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, to go wrong.

clue.text: Old magazine copies son returned?

parts.note: NOS, short for numbers, written back to front spells son

explanation.surface: A parent asks for old magazines from a son who has come home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: abbreviated numbers (NOS) put back give SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Back numbers are earlier issues of a periodical, no longer current.

clue.text: Fish, part of free lunch

indicators.note: the answer is part of these words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Fish is served as part of a free lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Avoid having nasty pest on team

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on another; here the scrambled letters follow the team

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team tries to steer clear of an obnoxious member.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to evade or dodge it.

clue.text: Sister pens story that's less original

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the sister's letters surround the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A nun writes a tale that is rather derivative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing; it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Staler means more hackneyed or tired, the opposite of fresh and novel.
